plugin_desc: Huawei NetEngine SNMP collection for NE-series routers. In addition to standard IF-MIB interface metrics and 64-bit HC traffic counters, it collects entity CPU/memory/temperature/fan/optical/voltage health, device CPU duty and 64-bit memory, PSU and fan presence, board and chassis power, forwarding usage, slot status, IF-EXT rates, BGP peer state and session counts, VRF count, and BFD session state. Supported brands/models include Huawei NetEngine NE40E and related NE-series routers (sysObjectID family 1.3.6.1.4.1.2011.2.62 and 1.3.6.1.4.1.2011.2.297).
name: Router

metrics.name: snmp_uptime
metrics.description: This metric indicates the uptime of the device since the last restart. By monitoring the uptime, network administrators can understand the stability and reliability of the device and identify potential reboot or failure issues.

metrics.name: device_cpu_usage
metrics.description: Per-entity CPU utilization of the Huawei NE device control plane (hwEntityCpuUsage), normalized to a 0-100 percentage. Dimension descr is entPhysicalName. Sustained high CPU usage can indicate control-plane overload, routing instability, or attack traffic, and may lead to slow management response or packet processing delays.

metrics.name: device_memory_usage
metrics.description: Per-entity memory utilization of the Huawei NE device (hwEntityMemUsage), reported directly as a 0-100 percentage. Dimension descr is entPhysicalName. High memory usage may indicate memory leaks, oversized routing tables, or insufficient capacity, and can cause instability or failed allocations.

metrics.name: device_temperature_celsius
metrics.description: This metric reports the temperature reading of each Huawei hardware sensor (hwEntityTemperature), in degrees Celsius. Abnormally high temperatures may indicate fan failure, blocked airflow, or excessive ambient heat, and can trigger thermal protection or hardware damage if left unaddressed.

metrics.name: device_voltage_volts
metrics.description: Per-entity input voltage of the Huawei NE device (hwEntityVoltage). The device reports millivolts; the query divides by 1000 to display volts. Values outside the rated range may indicate unstable power and hardware risk.

metrics.name: device_fan_state
metrics.description: This metric reports the operational state of each Huawei cooling fan (hwEntityFanState). A non-normal state indicates a cooling fault that can quickly lead to overheating and should be investigated immediately.

metrics.name: device_optical_rx_power
metrics.description: Per-module SFP/optical receive power in dBm (hwEntityOpticalRxPower). The device reports uW; Telegraf stores raw uW and this query converts with 10*log10(uW/1000), dropping <=0 (invalid/no-module). Dimension descr is entPhysicalName. A dropping RX level is an early sign of fiber attenuation, dirty optics, or a failing peer transmitter.

metrics.name: device_optical_tx_power
metrics.description: Per-module SFP/optical transmit power in dBm (hwEntityOpticalTxPower). The device reports uW; Telegraf stores raw uW and this query converts with 10*log10(uW/1000), dropping <=0 (invalid/no-module). Dimension descr is entPhysicalName. An abnormally low TX level indicates a failing laser/optic rather than fiber attenuation alone.

metrics.name: device_cpu_dev_duty
metrics.description: Instantaneous CPU duty of each Huawei NE CPU device entry (hwCpuDevDuty), reported as a 0-100 percentage. Complements per-entity hwEntityCpuUsage for control-plane load on NetEngine platforms.

metrics.name: device_cpu_dev_avg_duty_1min
metrics.description: One-minute average CPU duty of each Huawei NE CPU device entry (hwAvgDuty1min), reported as a 0-100 percentage. Use this to smooth short spikes when judging control-plane pressure.

metrics.name: device_cpu_dev_avg_duty_5min
metrics.description: Five-minute average CPU duty of each Huawei NE CPU device entry (hwAvgDuty5min), reported as a 0-100 percentage. Sustained elevation points to lasting control-plane load rather than a brief burst.

metrics.name: device_memory_dev_size
metrics.description: Total memory size of each Huawei NE memory device entry (hwMemoryDevSize64), in bytes. Together with free memory it shows capacity remaining on the forwarding/control memory pool.

metrics.name: device_memory_dev_free
metrics.description: Free memory of each Huawei NE memory device entry (hwMemoryDevFree64), in bytes. Persistently low free memory indicates rising memory pressure and risk of allocation failure.

metrics.name: device_psu_state
metrics.description: Operational state of each Huawei NE power supply (hwEntityPwrState). A non-normal state signals a power redundancy or hardware fault; on devices with redundant PSUs a single failure may not cause an outage but removes redundancy and must be remediated promptly.

metrics.name: device_psu_present
metrics.description: Presence of each Huawei NE power supply (hwEntityPwrPresent). Absent means the slot is empty or the module was pulled; combined with PSU state this confirms lost redundancy.

metrics.name: device_fan_speed
metrics.description: Fan rotation speed of each Huawei NE cooling fan (hwEntityFanSpeed). Abnormally low or zero speed indicates a stalled or failed fan and a risk of overheating; abnormally high speed may indicate the device is compensating for high temperature.

metrics.name: device_fan_present
metrics.description: Presence of each Huawei NE cooling fan (hwEntityFanPresent). Absent means the fan tray is missing; investigate immediately because cooling capacity is reduced.

metrics.name: device_entity_board_power
metrics.description: Board power consumption of each Huawei NE entity (hwEntityBoardPower), in watts. Unexpected rise can indicate a failing board, abnormal traffic load, or a cooling problem that increases power draw.

metrics.name: device_power_used
metrics.description: Chassis-level used power of the Huawei NE device (hwDevicePowerInfoUsedPower), in watts. Rising used power against a stable total budget indicates growing load or a hardware inefficiency.

metrics.name: device_power_total
metrics.description: Chassis-level total power capacity of the Huawei NE device (hwDevicePowerInfoTotalPower), in watts. Used as the denominator when judging how close the chassis is to its power budget.

metrics.name: device_forward_performance_usage
metrics.description: Forwarding performance usage of the Huawei NE device (hwEntityForwardPerformanceUsage), as a 0-100 percentage. High values mean the forwarding engine is close to its capacity and new traffic may be delayed or dropped.

metrics.name: device_fwd_cpu_usage
metrics.description: Forwarding-plane CPU usage of the Huawei NE device (hwFwdCpuUsageRate), as a 0-100 percentage. Sustained high forwarding CPU can cause packet delay, drops, or protocol flapping.

metrics.name: device_entity_oper_status
metrics.description: Operational status of each Huawei NE entity (hwEntityOperStatus). Disabled or offline entities should be correlated with standby status and slot state to locate failed boards.

metrics.name: device_entity_standby_status
metrics.description: Standby status of each Huawei NE entity (hwEntityStandbyStatus). Unexpected loss of providingService or hotStandby on a redundant board indicates a switchover or a failed standby.

metrics.name: device_optical_temperature
metrics.description: Temperature of each Huawei NE optical module (hwEntityOpticalTemperature), in degrees Celsius. High module temperature accelerates laser aging and can precede optical power failure.

metrics.name: device_optical_bias
metrics.description: Laser bias current of each Huawei NE optical module (hwEntityOpticalBiasCurrent). Drift away from the normal range is an early sign of a failing transmitter.

metrics.name: device_optical_voltage
metrics.description: Supply voltage of each Huawei NE optical module (hwEntityOpticalVoltage). The device reports millivolts; the query divides by 1000 to display volts. Out-of-range voltage can cause unstable optics.

metrics.name: device_slot_oper_status
metrics.description: Operational status of each Huawei NE slot (hwSlotOperStatus). A down slot means the card is missing, powered off, or failed, which can drop all interfaces on that slot.

metrics.name: interface_ifAdminStatus
metrics.description: This metric indicates the administrative status of the network interface.

metrics.name: interface_ifOperStatus
metrics.description: This metric reflects the actual operational status of the network interface.

metrics.name: interface_ifSpeed
metrics.description: This metric indicates the maximum data transmission speed supported by the network interface.

metrics.name: interface_ifHighSpeed
metrics.description: Interface speed in megabits per second from IF-MIB ifHighSpeed. Used together with ifSpeed so high-rate NetEngine ports are not capped by the 32-bit ifSpeed gauge.

metrics.name: interface_ifInErrors
metrics.description: This metric calculates the average rate of incoming error packets over the past 5 minutes.

metrics.name: interface_ifOutErrors
metrics.description: This metric calculates the average rate of outgoing error packets over the past 5 minutes.

metrics.name: interface_ifInDiscards
metrics.description: This metric represents the average rate of incoming discarded packets over the past 5 minutes.

metrics.name: interface_ifOutDiscards
metrics.description: This metric calculates the average rate of outgoing discarded packets over the past 5 minutes.

metrics.name: interface_ifInUcastPkts
metrics.description: This metric indicates the average rate of incoming unicast packets over the past 5 minutes.

metrics.name: interface_ifOutUcastPkts
metrics.description: This metric calculates the average rate of outgoing unicast packets over the past 5 minutes.

metrics.name: interface_ifInOctets
metrics.description: This metric indicates the average rate of bytes received over the past 5 minutes.

metrics.name: interface_ifOutOctets
metrics.description: This metric calculates the average rate of bytes sent over the past 5 minutes.

metrics.name: interface_ifHCInOctets
metrics.description: This metric indicates the average rate of bytes received over the past 5 minutes, based on the 64-bit ifHCInOctets counter which does not wrap on high-speed interfaces.

metrics.name: interface_ifHCOutOctets
metrics.description: This metric calculates the average rate of bytes sent over the past 5 minutes, based on the 64-bit ifHCOutOctets counter which does not wrap on high-speed interfaces.

metrics.name: device_total_incoming_traffic
metrics.description: This metric indicates the average rate of total bytes received by the entire device over the past 5 minutes.

metrics.name: device_total_outgoing_traffic
metrics.description: This metric represents the average rate of total bytes sent by the entire device over the past 5 minutes.

metrics.name: interface_ext_input_octet_rate
metrics.description: Instantaneous inbound octet rate of each Huawei NE interface (hwIFExtInputOctetRate). Unlike counter-based IF-MIB rates, this is a device-computed gauge and is useful for spotting bursts between poll intervals.

metrics.name: interface_ext_output_octet_rate
metrics.description: Instantaneous outbound octet rate of each Huawei NE interface (hwIFExtOutputOctetRate). Use it with the inbound rate to see whether a port is congested in one direction.

metrics.name: interface_ext_input_pkt_rate
metrics.description: Instantaneous inbound packet rate of each Huawei NE interface (hwIFExtInputPktRate). A high packet rate with modest octet rate often indicates small-packet pressure.

metrics.name: interface_ext_output_pkt_rate
metrics.description: Instantaneous outbound packet rate of each Huawei NE interface (hwIFExtOutputPktRate). Combined with error and discard rates it helps separate congestion from physical faults.

metrics.name: interface_ext_flow_status
metrics.description: Flow status of each Huawei NE interface (hwIFExtFlowStatus). Abnormal flow status means the interface is up but traffic is blocked or rate-limited and should be checked together with QoS and protocol state.

metrics.name: device_bgp_peer_state
metrics.description: State of each Huawei NE BGP peer (hwBgpPeerState). Established is the healthy state; idle, active, or connect for a configured peer indicates a session that failed to come up or flapped.

metrics.name: device_bgp_peer_established_time
metrics.description: Time the Huawei NE BGP peer has stayed in Established (hwBgpPeerFsmEstablishedTime), in seconds. A sudden drop to near zero means the session reset; correlate with peer state.

metrics.name: device_bgp_peer_session_num
metrics.description: Total BGP peer session count on the Huawei NE device (hwBgpPeerSessionNum). A sudden drop can mean multiple peers went down together.

metrics.name: device_bgp_ibgp_session_num
metrics.description: IBGP session count on the Huawei NE device (hwBgpPeerIBgpSessionNum). Loss of IBGP sessions can partition the IGP/BGP design inside an AS.

metrics.name: device_bgp_ebgp_session_num
metrics.description: EBGP session count on the Huawei NE device (hwBgpPeerEBgpSessionNum). Loss of EBGP sessions can withdraw external prefixes and shift traffic.

metrics.name: device_vrf_count
metrics.description: Number of configured VRFs on the Huawei NE device (hwConfiguredVrfs). Unexpected change can mean a VPN configuration rollback or a failed commit.

metrics.name: device_bfd_sess_state
metrics.description: State of each Huawei NE BFD session (hwBfdSessState). Down or init on a previously up session is an early sign of a forwarding-path failure, often before the routing protocol times out.

metrics.name: device_bfd_sess_act_number
metrics.description: Number of active BFD sessions on the Huawei NE device (hwBfdSessActNumber). A sudden drop means multiple sessions went down and routing reconvergence may follow.
